quotes.text: ClinEnv is built from MIMIC-IV v3.1 ( Johnson et al., 2023a ) and MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2 ( Johnson et al., 2023b ).
Because every stage is built deterministically from logged events, the ground truth can always be traced back to the originating row.

rationale: The paper names the source datasets with versions (MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2) and the PhysioNet platform. It gives a route from each task to its source record through subject_id/hadm_id keys, event provenance and row-level traceability of ground truth.

quotes.text: ClinEnv is derived from MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Note, which are de-identified and distributed through PhysioNet under a credentialed data use agreement

rationale: Origin (MIMIC-IV, one US academic medical center) and terms (credentialed DUA, de-identified) are stated. No consent or IRB status, and no explicit 'not required', is given, and the original collection method is not described, so the 2 anchor is not met.

quotes.text: We sample 3,509 admissions from 1,809 patients, keeping only admissions that produce at least one valid decision stage and stratifying by horizon

rationale: A sampling design (stratification by horizon, exclusion rules) and descriptive composition statistics (Table 4, Figures 4-5) are reported. There is no comparison against a named target population; the limitations note only the single-center source.

searched: S1 (results, limitations, ethical considerations), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 evaluation code, S5 prompts. No dedicated unsafe-output test or bias/subgroup fairness test is reported; the ethics section only states that scores do not imply safe or equitable behavior.

quotes.text: Must meet PhysioNet’s compliance standards before use.
Proprietary LLMs were accessed under a Zero Data Retention Policy required by PhysioNet.

rationale: Credentialed gated access via PhysioNet and a zero-data-retention requirement for proprietary APIs are developer-side controls. No measured contamination or overlap check is reported, so the 2 anchor is not met.

quotes.text: This separation prevents coded outcomes and discharge summaries from being passively exposed to the model while still making them available for planning and scoring.
diagnosis-code rows become held-out diagnosis candidates

rationale: The appendix states that coded outcomes and discharge notes are separated from the event timeline and not exposed to the model, and names mechanisms: held-out ground-truth items in the prepared case, role-restricted readviews, anchor-range expansion. The paper discloses that prior-stage ground truth is injected into later contexts by design, so this is not flagged. The statement is phrased as preventing passive exposure rather than 'cannot reach'.

quotes.text: ClinEnv is built from MIMIC-IV v3.1 ( Johnson et al., 2023a ) and MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2 ( Johnson et al., 2023b ).
Otherwise, both names are resolved to ATC codes via the RxNorm API.

rationale: Source data are version-pinned, but evaluation relies on live external services (the RxNorm API, embedding retrieval and LLM rerankers/judges) and the environment agents and judge are identified only by family name in the paper. This matches the 1 anchor: data pinned, evaluators or services live or unpinned.

searched: S1 (construction, appendix D construction quality), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No scripted reference solution run through the grader and no manual or agent-based solvability check is reported; construction quality is argued 'by construction' only.

searched: S1 (3.4, C.5, C.6), S4/S5 environment_controller and env_tools. No task changes environment state: submissions are recorded and scored, and later stages are given the ground-truth decisions rather than the model's earlier submissions, so the NA clause applies.

searched: S1 (scoring, results, limitations), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, no chance rate per metric and no design argument that trivial outputs would fail are given. The exact submission-count hint and ontology partial credit would affect chance level but this is not discussed.
searched: S1 tables 5, 6, 11, 12 and appendix G, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. Only seven LLMs are evaluated; no do-nothing or random agent score is reported.

searched: S1 (section 5, appendix C.7, D.2), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4 evaluation code, S5 judge prompts. The ICD reranker, drug mapping and coverage judge are LLM- or retrieval-based, but no agreement or error figures and no tests or reference-solution evidence are reported. Appendix D.2 describes ground-truth construction, not evaluator validation.

quotes.text: extra_kwargs: dict = {"tool_choice": "auto", "temperature": 0, "parallel_tool_calls": False}

rationale: Temperature 0 is set in the harness code, and the paper limits the agent to one tool call per turn. Neither S1-S3 nor the README states seeds, temperature or a repeated-run policy, so the safeguard is visible only in code.

quotes.text: Shaded bands are standard errors.

rationale: Standard errors appear on the per-stage curves in Figure 2. The headline model comparison in Table 5 has no CI or significance test. Claims such as 'GPT-5.4 leads on every outcome metric' are untested.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks). No number of runs per task, no seed or decoding policy and no statement of run independence appear in S1-S3. Temperature 0 is only in code (S4), which does not count.

quotes.text: Shaded bands are standard errors.

rationale: Standard errors are given only on the per-stage curves in Figure 2; Table 5 headline scores carry no CI or SE. The resampling unit is not named and clustering of stages within admissions or patients is not addressed.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4. No rerun, repeat-run variation, pass^k metric or action- or state-level agreement across reruns is reported.

searched: S1, S2, S4, S5. The paper names models by family only (GPT-5.4, Llama-3.1-70B, Gemma-3-27B). The README gives a snapshot (gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17) for one default model, but S1 names Claude-Sonnet-4.6 as the planner while config/planner.json lists gpt-5.4, an S1/S4 mismatch that counts as absent. No decoding parameters or harness commit are stated in S1-S3.

"drug_name": {"type": "string", "description": "Standard drug name."},
Ask the patient a question about their symptoms, history, or concerns.

contradiction_quotes.text: submit_plan | Both | Submit other management decision

rationale: JSON schemas exist for the nine tools in the agent-visible tool definitions, and Table 3 separates information-gathering tools from decision-submission and stage-advancing tools; tool descriptions reaching the agent also distinguish asking from submitting. Return and error semantics are documented only for the lab agent (null response). Table 3 lists submit_plan, which the code does not expose, so a flag is raised.

quotes.text: Simulates subjective patient reporting in lay language
each powered by GPT-5.4-mini and restricted to a designated readview

rationale: The paper discloses that the patient, nurse, lab and history tools are served by LLM agents (GPT-5.4-mini) over restricted readviews. No tests or conformance checks of tool behavior are reported. The tool descriptions and system prompt shown to the agent do not say the responders are simulated.

quotes.text: decisions are sequential and irreversible
Tests ordered beyond those evidenced in the ground-truth clinical picture are treated as unnecessary expenditure

rationale: Submissions and lab orders represent clinical orders, so the item applies. The paper frames decisions as irreversible and identifies the submit tools, and it scores unnecessary lab orders (waste) and drug cost. It does not state whether writes are executed, simulated or sandboxed, and this is not conveyed to the agent.

quotes.text: scoring each decision deterministically against structured EHR ground truth via Hungarian matching and ontology-based partial credit
a judge is given the complete readview

rationale: Grader inputs are stated: submitted free-text decisions matched to ICD/ATC ground truth, and an LLM judge over the readview and dialogue for coverage. A rationale for non-state grading is given (deterministic scoring versus LLM-as-judge). No validation on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates is reported.

quotes.text: Leakage expansion: after a single anchor is found, a local scan examines up to 10 events before and after the anchor.

rationale: Leakage controls exist at the tool and context level (leakage expansion of anchors, role-restricted readviews, prior admissions limited to earlier ones, lab agent returns null for tests not on record). There is no held-out or private split of labels beyond credentialed access, and no canary or provenance marker.

quotes.text: but on management stages F1 collapses to 0.13

rationale: Results are reported by decision type (diagnosis, medication, procedure; diagnosis-only versus management stages), by stage index and by horizon subset. No results by patient subgroup are reported although MIMIC holds demographic fields. Slice sizes appear in Table 4, not alongside the slice results.

quotes.text: ClinEnv is derived from MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Note, which are de-identified and distributed through PhysioNet under a credentialed data use agreement
require users to hold the appropriate PhysioNet credentials

rationale: The source is stated as real de-identified MIMIC-IV data, governed by a PhysioNet credentialed DUA. Data access terms (PhysioNet credentialing) are stated separately from the GitHub code repository; no code licence is given in the packet.
